docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: WhisperJAV 1.10 runs on Windows, Linux and Apple silicon Macs. Choose the way of installing that fits your computer.

docs.title: Which install method should I use?
docs.text:
If you... Use this Just want it to work (Windows) Windows Installer Manage your own Python environment on Windows Windows Python Install Have an Apple silicon Mac (M1 or newer) macOS Guide Run Linux Linux Guide

Coming from 1.9.x? Install the newest 1.10 release fresh. 1.10 needs Python 3.13, so whisperjav-upgrade cannot take a 1.9.x install to 1.10. Your settings in the user settings folder are kept.

Google Colab and Kaggle are not supported by 1.10: it is made and tested for installs on your own computer only. The Colab expert notebook keeps installing 1.9.5.

docs.title: Accelerated or not
docs.text:
A GPU — a graphics card, or the GPU inside an Apple chip — does the heavy work of turning speech into text many times faster than the CPU. Each WhisperJAV install is made for one accelerator, which you choose when you install: NVIDIA GPU (CUDA), GPU through Vulkan (AMD, Intel or older NVIDIA card, Windows), Apple GPU (Metal), your own PyTorch, or CPU only (not accelerated). At the start of a run, WhisperJAV says where each part runs whenever the install's GPU is not in use. Not accelerated works, but several times slower.

What each computer gets:

Your computer The install is made for GGUF pipelines (the nine run by CrispASR) All other pipelines Windows PC with an NVIDIA GPU that 1.10 supports (GTX 16 / RTX 20 or newer), driver 580 or newer NVIDIA GPU (CUDA), chosen by itself NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) Windows PC with an AMD or Intel graphics card, or an NVIDIA card older than 1.10 supports GPU through Vulkan, your own PyTorch, or CPU only — the installer asks GPU through Vulkan: your graphics card (experimental, not tested) CPU (not accelerated), several times slower Windows PC without a graphics card WhisperJAV can use CPU only — the installer asks CPU (not accelerated) CPU (not accelerated) Linux PC with a supported NVIDIA GPU, driver 570 or newer NVIDIA GPU (CUDA), chosen by itself NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) on x86-64; CPU on ARM64 NVIDIA GPU (CUDA); on ARM64, balanced, fast and faster on the CPU Linux PC with an AMD or Intel GPU, or no GPU your own PyTorch, or CPU only — the installer asks CPU (not accelerated) your own PyTorch: as below; CPU only: CPU (not accelerated) Apple silicon Mac, macOS 14 or newer Apple GPU (Metal), chosen by itself ask for the Apple GPU (Metal) — not yet tested on a Mac transformers: Apple GPU (Metal); fidelity: asks for it, not yet tested on a Mac; balanced, fast, faster and ChronosJAV: CPU (not accelerated) Any supported computer with your own PyTorch build for your GPU (for example ROCm for an AMD GPU) Own PyTorch: WhisperJAV installs everything except PyTorch Windows: asks for your graphics card through Vulkan (experimental, not tested); Linux: CPU; Mac: asks for the Apple GPU (Metal), not yet tested on a Mac fidelity, transformers, ChronosJAV and the speech enhancers ask for the GPU your PyTorch reports (not tested); balanced, fast and faster run on the CPU unless CTranslate2, their engine, sees an NVIDIA GPU

The WhisperSeg speech segmenter runs on the CPU in every install.

Changing the accelerator later: run the installer again. It shows the choice, with the accelerator of your install pre-selected. whisperjav-upgrade never changes it.

One run on the CPU: add --device cpu to that run. In the GUI, the Customize window of an Ensemble pass has a Device menu; "CPU (not accelerated)" puts that pass on the CPU (not offered for the GGUF pipelines). When the GPU of an NVIDIA GPU install cannot be used, the GUI offers "Run on the CPU this time".

Intel GPUs in WhisperJAV 1.10: on Windows, the GGUF pipelines can use an Intel GPU through Vulkan — experimental, not tested. WhisperJAV 1.10 does not use Intel GPUs through PyTorch (Intel's XPU builds): with such a PyTorch, the other pipelines run on the CPU.

Experimental: GPUs through Vulkan on Windows, and your own PyTorch, are experimental in WhisperJAV 1.10: we have done everything we can to make them work, but we could not test them on AMD or Intel graphics cards. Please tell us how they work on your PC: https://github.com/meizhong986/WhisperJAV/issues

docs.title: Supported computers
docs.text:
Every installer checks the computer before anything is installed. On a computer outside this list it says why and installs nothing.

WhisperJAV 1.10 supports Not supported Windows Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (x86-64) Windows on ARM (for example Snapdragon laptops); Windows older than 10 Linux x86-64 or ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, Debian 12 or newer, Fedora 36 or newer, openSUSE Leap 15.6, and distributions built on them; rolling distributions glibc older than 2.35: Ubuntu 20.04, Debian 11, openSUSE Leap 15.5 (glibc 2.31); Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 9 (glibc 2.34) Mac Apple silicon (M1 or newer), macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer Intel Macs; macOS 13 and older NVIDIA GPU, for the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) install GTX 16 / RTX 20 series or newer; driver 580 or newer on Windows, 570 or newer on Linux An older card or driver can still install: the installer offers the other accelerators Python (source install) 3.13 other versions Hosted notebooks — Google Colab, Kaggle

The GGUF pipelines (all nine) need a processor with AVX2 (Intel since 2013, AMD since 2015); every other pipeline runs without it.

Other needs: 8 GB of RAM (16 GB recommended); about 10 GB of free disk space for the install and the models it downloads on first use; FFmpeg (the Windows installer brings it); an internet connection while installing and on the first run of each model.

After installation, launch the GUI with whisperjav-gui and follow the GUI User Guide.

docs.title: WhisperJAV GUI User Guide
docs.text: Screenshots from v1.8.10 · Windows 11

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Launching the App
  2. Interface Overview
  3. Adding Files
  4. Choosing an Output Location
  5. Basic Transcription
  6. Advanced Options
  7. Ensemble Mode (Two-Pass)
  8. AI Subtitle Translation
  9. Running a Job
  10. Console Output
  11. Menus & Dialogs
  12. Keyboard Shortcuts
  13. Common Workflows

docs.title: 1. Launching the App
docs.text:
After installation, launch WhisperJAV from:

  • Desktop shortcut — created automatically by the installer
  • Start menu — search "WhisperJAV"
  • Command line — whisperjav-gui

When the window opens, WhisperJAV checks only that the GUI's own parts are installed, and on Windows the WebView2 runtime. whisperjav --check on the command line checks the rest of the install (Python, PyTorch and the GPU, FFmpeg, CrispASR and its models). The start of every run checks that this install's GPU can be used (see When a run does not start).

docs.title: 2. Interface Overview
docs.text:
The GUI is divided into five areas, top to bottom:

Area Purpose Header bar Language button (English / 中文), theme button (4 themes, and Check for Updates), and an update notice when a new version is out Source Add video/audio files to process Destination Where to save output SRT files Options tabs Four tabs of configuration (see sections 5–8) Run controls & Console Progress bar, Start/Cancel, and real-time log output

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
Click the palette icon in the header to open the theme menu:

Theme Description Default Light theme with blue accents Google Material Design inspired Carbon IBM Carbon dark theme Primer GitHub-style neutral palette

docs.title: Interface language (English / 中文)
docs.text:
The 中文 button in the header, next to the palette icon, switches the window to Simplified Chinese. In Chinese the button reads English and switches back. The change is immediate; the file list and a run in progress are not affected.

  • In Chinese: tabs, buttons, menus, tooltips, pop-up boxes, Customize Parameters and Translation Settings.
  • Stays English: the console, file names, the messages written while files are processed, and the Parameter Guide page.
  • The language is kept for the next start, whether or not Remember settings is ticked. On Windows, the very first start follows the display language: Chinese when Windows is set to Chinese, English otherwise.

docs.title: 3. Adding Files
docs.text: WhisperJAV takes video files ending in .mp4, .mkv, .avi, .mov, .wmv, .flv, .webm, .m4v, .mpg or .mpeg, and audio files ending in .mp3, .wav, .flac, .aac, .ogg, .wma, .m4a, .m4b or .opus. Files with other endings are skipped.

docs.title: Adding files
docs.text:
• Drag and drop files directly onto the file list area
  • Add File(s) button — opens a multi-select file dialog
  • Add Folder button — adds the folder to the list; the run then takes every media file in it and in its sub-folders

Each file or folder appears in the list with its full path.

docs.title: Managing the file list
docs.text:
• Remove Selected — removes highlighted files from the list
  • Clear — removes all files

docs.title: 4. Choosing an Output Location
docs.text:
By default, SRT files are saved next to the source video. Uncheck "Save next to source video" to pick a custom output folder.

Setting Behavior Checked (default) Output SRT saved in the same folder as each source video Unchecked All SRT files saved to the chosen output directory

When unchecked, use Browse to select a folder, or Open to view it in File Explorer.

docs.title: 5. Basic Transcription
docs.text: The Transcription Mode tab (Tab 1) controls the core transcription pipeline.

docs.title: Mode
docs.text:
Selects the processing pipeline. Each mode trades speed for accuracy.

Mode Backend Scene Detection VAD Best For Fidelity Whisper Yes Full Maximum accuracy, slow Balanced (default) Whisper Yes Yes General use Fast Whisper Yes No Quick results with scene awareness Faster Faster-Whisper No No Maximum speed, minimal processing Transformers HuggingFace No (by default) No Alternative backend

docs.title: Sensitivity
docs.text:
Controls how aggressively the system detects and segments speech.

Sensitivity Description Aggressive (default) Lower thresholds, captures more speech including quiet passages Balanced Middle ground Conservative Higher thresholds, fewer false positives, may miss quiet speech

docs.title: Source Language
docs.text:
The language spoken in the video. Affects Whisper's language hint and post-processing rules.

  • Japanese (default) — optimized with Japanese-specific regrouping, particle detection, aizuchi handling
  • Korean, Chinese, English — standard Whisper processing

docs.title: Subtitle Output
docs.text:
• Native (default) — subtitles in the original spoken language
  • Direct-to-English — Whisper translates to English during transcription (lower quality than dedicated translation)

Known issue: with Kotoba Bilingual v1.0, the default model of the transformers pipeline, the model gives the English text no times, so the subtitles are unusable.

docs.title: 6. Advanced Options
docs.text:
The Transcription Adv. Options tab (Tab 2) provides additional controls for troubleshooting and fine-tuning.

Option Default Description Model override Off When checked, forces a specific Whisper model size instead of the pipeline default Model dropdown large-v2 Greyed out until Model override is ticked. Options: large-v2, large-v3, turbo Output format SRT Output format: SRT, VTT, or Both Async processing Off Enables asynchronous pipeline execution Debug logging Off Shows WhisperJAV's debug lines in the console and keeps the metadata files in the temp folder (same as --debug) Keep temp files Off Preserves intermediate audio chunks and processing artifacts Temp dir System default Where a run's intermediate files go; they are removed at the end unless Keep temp files is ticked

docs.title: 7. Ensemble Mode (Two-Pass)
docs.text: The Ensemble Mode tab (Tab 3) runs one or two pipelines on each file; with Pass 2 ticked, the two passes' subtitles are merged into one file.

docs.title: How Ensemble Works
docs.text:
1. Pass 1 processes the video with one pipeline configuration
  2. Pass 2 (optional) processes the same video with a different configuration
  3. The two SRT outputs are merged using a configurable strategy

docs.title: Pass Configuration
docs.text:
Always active. Each pass has identical controls:

Control Options Default Pipeline Whisper-Based: Balanced, Fast, Faster, Fidelity; HuggingFace: Transformers (HF); ChronosJAV: Qwen3-ASR, Anime-Whisper; External (BYOP): XXL Faster Whisper; GGUF via crispasr: parakeet, cohere; Experimental, open to feedback: reazonspeech, kotoba, whisper-turbo, whisper-large, MOSS, haas, qwen3-asr Pass 1: cohere; Pass 2: parakeet (off until ticked) Sensitivity Aggressive, Balanced, Conservative set when you choose the pipeline: Pass 1 (cohere) Balanced, Pass 2 (parakeet) Aggressive Scene Detector Auditok, Silero, Semantic, None Semantic Speech Enhancer None; Vocal Separation: Mel-Band-RoFormer, Mini-BS-RoFormer, htdemucs (Demucs v4); Noise Suppression: ZipEnhancer; DSP: FFmpeg Audio Filters... None Speech Segmenter FireRedVAD, TEN VAD, WhisperSeg (JA-ASMR), Silero v3.1, Silero v4.0, Silero v6.2; under "Experimental, open to feedback": Sortformer (NVIDIA Nemotron), pyannote 3.0; None. For Balanced, the Silero version of its built-in VAD: 3.1, 4.0 (default), 6.2; for a GGUF pass, None sends each scene to the model whole. set when you choose the pipeline: Pass 1 (cohere) FireRedVAD, Pass 2 (parakeet) TEN VAD Model the models of the chosen pipeline the pipeline's default

docs.title: Available Pipelines
docs.text:
The pipeline dropdown groups options by backend:

  • Whisper-Based: Balanced, Fast, Faster, Fidelity
  • HuggingFace: Transformers
  • ChronosJAV: Qwen3-ASR, Anime-Whisper
  • GGUF via crispasr: parakeet (Parakeet-CrispASR), cohere (Cohere-CrispASR); below a divider line, Experimental, open to feedback: reazonspeech (ReazonSpeech-CrispASR), kotoba (Kotoba-CrispASR), whisper-turbo (Whisper-Turbo-CrispASR), whisper-large (Whisper-Large-CrispASR), MOSS (MOSS-CrispASR), haas (Haas-CrispASR), qwen3-asr (Qwen3-ASR-CrispASR) — Japanese only, all experimental; parakeet and cohere since 1.10.0, haas and qwen3-asr new in 1.10.2, the other five new in 1.10.1 (see GGUF pipelines (CrispASR))
  • External (BYOP): XXL Faster Whisper (Pass 1, Pass 2 or both)

docs.title: Customize Parameters
docs.text:
Click the Customize Parameters button on a pass to open its settings window. Its tabs depend on the pass's pipeline (below).

The tabs depend on the pass's pipeline: Model, Quality, Segmenter, Enhancer and Scene for Balanced, Fast, Faster and Fidelity; Model, Quality, Chunking, Enhancer and Scene for Transformers; Model, Audio, Generation, Alignment and Output for Qwen3-ASR and Anime-Whisper; the GGUF passes are described below. For XXL Faster Whisper the button is greyed out: XXL uses its own settings. A badge shows DEFAULT or CUSTOM to indicate whether parameters have been modified.

The Model tab has a Device menu: Auto (the GPU when one can be used, else the CPU) (the default), NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) or CPU (not accelerated).

For a GGUF pass (any pipeline under GGUF via crispasr or Experimental, open to feedback), the modal has four tabs: Segmenter, Enhancer, Scene and Timing; for MOSS (MOSS-CrispASR) it also has a MOSS tab. They start from the values the pass runs with. A status panel under the pass row shows the model (downloaded or not) and where CrispASR will run, for example "GPU: asks for the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA)". The Timing tab has one menu, Word timestamps: From the model or From the aligner (wav2vec2-ja), with the pipeline's default marked "(default)". When the pass's subtitle times come from the aligner (the default for cohere, or any GGUF pass set to From the aligner), the status panel also lists the aligner.

For a ChronosJAV pass (Qwen3-ASR, Anime-Whisper), the Alignment tab sets the subtitle timing (see Subtitle timing):

Control Options Default Aligner Backend CrispASR (GGUF, recommended), Qwen3 ForcedAligner (PyTorch), None (no aligner) CrispASR Aligner Model the models of the chosen backend: wav2vec2-ja (recommended), parakeet-ctc-ja (not recommended), qwen3-fa-gguf; or Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B (PyTorch) wav2vec2-ja Timestamp Mode Aligner + VAD Fallback, Aligner + Interpolation, Aligner Only (no recovery on collapse), VAD Only (no aligner loaded) VAD Only Timing Model (Whisper) Whisper small, None (no timing model) None Adaptive Step-Down a tick box not ticked

Since 1.10.1 the default is VAD Only with no timing model, ChronosJAV's timing of 1.9.5: no aligner is loaded, and the Aligner Backend, Aligner Model and Adaptive Step-Down controls are hidden until an aligner mode is chosen. With Aligner Backend None, the run uses VAD Only with Step-Down off, whatever Timestamp Mode and Adaptive Step-Down show. A status panel under a ChronosJAV pass row shows the CrispASR aligner and the timing model when the pass uses them (downloaded or not) and where CrispASR runs them. Since 1.10.0 the Alignment tab's values, and a preset saved from it, reach the run; from 1.8.10.post3 to 1.9.5 they were ignored.

At the bottom of the window, Save Preset saves this pass's settings (pipeline, sensitivity, scene detector, speech enhancer, speech segmenter, model and the window's values) under a name, and Load Preset... loads one into the pass. Presets are kept for the next start.

docs.title: Pass 2 Configuration
docs.text:
Check the Pass 2 checkbox to enable the second pass. Controls are identical to Pass 1.

When disabled, the row is greyed out and all controls are inactive.

docs.title: BYOP: XXL Faster Whisper (v1.8.9+; Pass 1 since 1.10.0)
docs.text:
Select XXL Faster Whisper as the pipeline of Pass 1, Pass 2 or both to use PurfView's Faster Whisper XXL as an external program. The menu lists it under External (BYOP): XXL is a separate program that you download yourself; WhisperJAV runs it.

When a pass is XXL, its Model column picks the Whisper model XXL runs, and a settings panel appears below the Pass 2 row:

Field Description Model (in the pass row) Large V2 (default), Large V3, Large V3 Turbo or Medium. XXL downloads the model the first time it is used. When both passes are XXL, each has its own model. Executable Path to your faster-whisper-xxl.exe. Click Browse to select it. Both passes use the same one. Extra Args Any additional flags to pass to XXL (default --verbose True --standard_asia). Choose the model in the Model column: a --model here is not used, and the console says so.

The other controls of an XXL pass (Sensitivity, Scene Detector, Speech Enhancer, Speech Segmenter, Customize) are greyed out: XXL uses its own settings. WhisperJAV sends XXL the input file, the output folder, the model, the language and the SRT output format (and --task translate when the subtitles are to be in English); you add any other XXL flags in the Extra Args field. XXL's real-time console output is streamed to the GUI console.

Before 1.10.0 the GUI sent no model to XXL, so XXL ran large-v3 even when Extra Args said --model large-v2 (#449).

If XXL fails for a file, the console says which pass failed and why. A failed Pass 1 marks the file failed; a failed Pass 2 leaves the file with Pass 1's subtitles, if Pass 1 made them. If XXL crashes during shutdown (a known ctranslate2 behavior) but the SRT was already written, WhisperJAV keeps the valid output instead of discarding it.

docs.title: Speech Enhancement: FFmpeg DSP
docs.text:
When FFmpeg DSP is selected as the speech enhancer, an additional panel appears with 8 audio processing effects:

Effect Description Loudness Normalization Normalize overall loudness to a standard level Dynamic Normalization Even out volume differences between quiet and loud sections Compression Reduce dynamic range Denoise Remove background noise High-pass Filter Remove low-frequency rumble Low-pass Filter Remove high-frequency hiss De-esser Reduce harsh sibilance (s/t sounds) Amplify Boost overall volume

docs.title: For VAD only (v1.8.10+)
docs.text: The Speech Enhancer menu ends, under a divider line, with the tick box For VAD only, ticked by default since 1.10.2. When ticked, the cleaned-up audio is used only to find the speech (VAD), and the original audio goes to the ASR model. Untick it to give the cleaned-up audio to the ASR model too. It takes effect with Fidelity, Qwen3-ASR, Anime-Whisper and the GGUF pipelines when a speech enhancer is chosen; it is not offered for Balanced, Fast, Faster, Transformers and XXL Faster Whisper, which keep one track.

docs.title: Merge Strategy
docs.text:
When Pass 2 is enabled, choose how the two outputs are combined:

Strategy (GUI) Command line What it does Pass 1 + Fill From Pass 2 (default) pass1_primary Keeps every Pass 1 subtitle; adds a Pass 2 subtitle only where it overlaps no Pass 1 subtitle Smart Merge smart_merge Pairs each Pass 1 subtitle with the Pass 2 subtitle that overlaps it most, if the overlap is at least 30% of the shorter one, and keeps one of the pair: the one with more of its own length inside the overlap; if that is about equal, the one with more text (a line of few different characters, such as ああああああああああ, counts as none); then the shorter one. Subtitles without a partner are kept from both passes Full Merge (All Lines) full_merge Keeps every subtitle of both passes, in time order; overlapping subtitles stay Pass 2 + Fill From Pass 1 pass2_primary As Pass 1 + Fill From Pass 2, with the passes swapped Pass 1 + Fill (30% Overlap) pass1_overlap Keeps every Pass 1 subtitle; adds a Pass 2 subtitle unless it overlaps a Pass 1 subtitle by more than 30% of that subtitle's length Pass 2 + Fill (30% Overlap) pass2_overlap As above, with the passes swapped — (command line only) longest Pairs subtitles as Smart Merge does and keeps the one with more text

With every strategy, a subtitle whose text is the same as the one just before it is then removed.

docs.title: Serial Mode
docs.text: Finish each file is ticked by default: each file is finished (Pass 1 → Pass 2 → Merge) before the next one starts, so a file's subtitles are ready as soon as it is done and a crash in one file does not lose the others. Untick it to run Pass 1 on all files, then Pass 2: each pass then starts once for all the files instead of once per file. With Remember settings on, the box keeps its state for the next start.

docs.title: Inline AI Translation (Ensemble)
docs.text: Check "AI-translate" after the merge strategy to automatically translate the merged output. This shows an inline provider/model selector and a settings button.

docs.title: 8. AI Subtitle Translation
docs.text: The AI SRT Translate tab (Tab 4) is a standalone tool for translating existing SRT files using AI language models.

docs.title: Provider & Model
docs.text:
Providers are grouped into Local LLM and Cloud AI in the dropdown.

Provider Notes Ollama Connects to your locally installed Ollama. Free, private, no API key. See below. DeepSeek Cloud API. Cost-effective, good quality for CJK languages. Gemini Google's API. Good multilingual support. Claude Anthropic's API. High quality, higher cost. GPT OpenAI's API. Widely available. OpenRouter Meta-router supporting many models. GLM Zhipu AI. Good for Chinese-related tasks. Groq Fast inference cloud provider. Custom Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Each provider populates a Model dropdown with available models. Use Override/Custom Model to specify a model ID not in the list.

docs.title: Ollama Integration (v1.8.10+)
docs.text:
WhisperJAV connects to your locally installed Ollama. You must install Ollama separately — WhisperJAV does not include it.

When you select Ollama as the provider, the GUI detects your setup and shows one of three panels:

State What you see What to do Not installed Download link and "Check Again" button Install Ollama from ollama.com, then click "Check Again" No model Recommended model with ollama pull command Copy the command and run it in your terminal, or select a model from the dropdown to download it Connected Green status dot, model dropdown populated Select a model and proceed

The model dropdown is split into two groups:

  • Installed Models — models already on your machine (shown with download sizes)
  • Recommendations — suggested models you haven't installed yet

Selecting an uninstalled model opens a download confirmation popup. The model is pulled directly from within the GUI.

VRAM-based recommendations:

GPU VRAM Recommended Model 4 GB gemma3:4b 8 GB qwen2.5:7b 12 GB gemma3:12b 16 GB+ qwen2.5:14b

After translation completes, WhisperJAV automatically unloads the model from VRAM so your GPU is free for other work.

If Ollama is installed but not running, the GUI starts the server automatically.

docs.title: API Key & Connection Test
docs.text:
For cloud providers, enter your API key and click Test Connection to verify it works. A status icon shows the result.

  • Green checkmark: connection successful
  • Red X: connection failed (check key and endpoint)

Ollama does not require an API key.

docs.title: Language & Tone
docs.text:
Setting Options Default Source Language Japanese, Korean, Chinese, English Japanese Target Language English, Chinese, Indonesian, Portuguese, Spanish, French, Italian, Thai, Korean English Tone/Style Standard, Adult (contextual), Adult/Explicit Standard

Standard tone produces clean, natural translations. Adult (contextual) uses explicit language only where the original line is explicit; neutral dialogue stays neutral. Adult/Explicit makes everything explicit, neutral dialogue too.

docs.title: Advanced Settings
docs.text:
Click the collapsible Advanced Settings section to reveal additional options:

Setting Default Description Movie Title (empty) Provides context to the AI for better translation Names (one per line) (empty) Character or actress names, for the AI to handle correctly Plot Summary (empty) Additional context for the AI translator Scene Threshold 60 sec How the translator groups subtitles into scenes for batch processing Max Batch Size 30 Maximum subtitles per translation batch Max Retries 3 Retry count for failed API calls Rate Limit (req/min) (empty; the field shows "No limit") Requests per minute limit Custom Endpoint (empty) Override the default API endpoint URL

docs.title: Translation Progress
docs.text: Translation has its own progress bar and Start/Cancel buttons at the bottom of Tab 4. The main Run Controls section is hidden while Tab 4 is active.

docs.title: Starting
docs.text:
1. Add one or more files (Section 3)
  2. Configure options on the relevant tab
  3. Click Start

While a run is going, the progress bar moves without a percentage and the status reads "Running..."; the console shows each step.

docs.title: Cancelling
docs.text: Click Cancel to stop the current job. The process terminates and any partial output is preserved.

docs.title: When processing is running
docs.text:
• All file selection and configuration controls are disabled
  • The Cancel button becomes active
  • Real-time progress appears in both the progress bar and the console

docs.title: Completion
docs.text: When the run ends, the status shows "Finished" with the number of files in each state (done, empty, suspect, failed, skipped), from the run summary in whisperjav_run.json. The output SRT is ready to use with any media player.

docs.title: When a run does not start
docs.text:
If a run stops before it processes anything, a dialog says why:

Dialog When What you can do The NVIDIA GPU cannot be used the install is made for the NVIDIA GPU, and the GPU cannot be used now (for example after a driver change) Run on the CPU this time runs the same job again on the CPU; Close leaves it. The dialog names the reason and the fix. The run did not start a setting the run cannot use, or PyTorch missing (for example on an Own PyTorch install before you added your PyTorch) the dialog says what to do; nothing was processed The run ended without a run summary WhisperJAV stopped unexpectedly files finished before that are in the output folder; the console shows what happened

When the install's GPU can be used (an NVIDIA GPU or Apple GPU install), nothing is shown at the start of a run. On every other install, the console shows where each part runs on this computer; the run then goes on.

docs.title: 10. Console Output
docs.text:
The console at the bottom shows real-time log messages from the processing pipeline.

Color Meaning Green Success messages (file saved, processing complete) Yellow Warnings (fallback activated, parameter adjusted) Red Errors (file not found, CUDA failure) White/Gray Informational messages (progress, stage transitions)

Click Clear to reset the console output.

Each run started from the Transcription Mode or Ensemble Mode tab also writes a log file, whisperjav_run.log, in a raw_subs folder next to the run's whisperjav_run.json: in the output folder, or, with Save next to source video, in the folder of the first file in the list (inside the folder, if the first entry is a folder). It holds WhisperJAV's lines, the debug lines included, and CrispASR's start-up lines. It leaves out the start banner, the RUN SUMMARY table (that is in whisperjav_run.json), the total processing time, the translation lines, other libraries' warnings and the lines of the balanced pipeline's ASR worker. Each Ensemble pass writes its own file beside it (whisperjav_run.pass1.log, whisperjav_run.pass2.log). Each run replaces the last run's log files.

docs.title: About Dialog
docs.text: Press F1, or click About at the bottom of the window. Shows version info, feature list, and keyboard shortcuts.

docs.title: Update Check
docs.text:
WhisperJAV checks for updates automatically on startup (after a 3-second delay). When a new version is available, a subtle indicator appears in the header bar showing the version number. Click it to view the changelog.

For critical updates, a full banner appears at the top of the window.

You can also check manually: click the palette icon in the header, then Check for Updates.

docs.title: Translation Settings Modal
docs.text: Accessible from the Translation Settings button in the Ensemble tab's AI-translate row. Provides the same configuration as Tab 4 in a compact modal.

docs.title: 12. Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+O Open file dialog (add files) Ctrl+R Start processing Escape Cancel current job / close dialogs F1 Open About dialog Arrow keys Navigate file list

docs.title: Quick Transcription
docs.text:
1. Drag a video file onto the app
  2. Leave defaults (Balanced mode, Aggressive sensitivity, Japanese)
  3. Click Start
  4. SRT appears next to your video file

docs.title: Two-Pass Transcription (Ensemble)
docs.text:
1. Add files
  2. Go to the Ensemble Mode tab
  3. Pass 1 starts on cohere (Balanced, Semantic, FireRedVAD); keep it or choose another pipeline
  4. Tick Pass 2 and choose its pipeline (it starts on parakeet)
  5. Under Merge, choose a strategy (default Pass 1 + Fill From Pass 2)
  6. Click Start
  7. Two passes run sequentially, then results are merged

docs.title: Transcribe + Translate in One Step
docs.text:
1. Add files
  2. Go to Ensemble tab
  3. Configure passes as desired
  4. Check "AI-translate"
  5. Select provider, enter API key if needed
  6. Click Start
  7. Get translated SRT automatically after transcription

docs.title: Translate an Existing SRT
docs.text:
1. Go to AI SRT Translate tab (Tab 4)
  2. Add your SRT file(s)
  3. Select provider and model
  4. Enter API key and test connection
  5. Set target language
  6. Click Start

docs.title: Translate with Ollama (Free, Local)
docs.text:
1. Install Ollama on your machine
  2. Go to AI SRT Translate tab (Tab 4)
  3. Select Ollama from the provider dropdown
  4. Wait for the green "connected" status
  5. Select or download a model (e.g., gemma3:4b for 4GB VRAM, qwen2.5:7b for 8GB)
  6. Add your SRT file(s) and click Start
  7. No API key or internet needed — everything runs locally on your GPU

docs.title: Without a GPU
docs.text: On an install made for the CPU only, there is nothing to tick: every run uses the CPU. Use Faster mode for the best speed. Processing is several times slower than on a GPU, but works. To run one pass on the CPU on a GPU install, choose CPU (not accelerated) as the Device in the Model tab of that pass's Customize Parameters window. A GGUF or XXL pass has no Device menu: it follows the whole run's device (--device on the command line).

docs.title: WhisperJAV Linux Installation Guide
docs.text:
Version: 1.10.2

Nobody in the project has run WhisperJAV 1.10 on Linux yet. Please tell us how it works for you: https://github.com/meizhong986/WhisperJAV/issues

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
1. Your computer
  2. System packages
  3. Python 3.13
  4. NVIDIA driver
  5. Installation
  6. What the install is made for
  7. Check and run
  8. Updating
  9. Troubleshooting
  10. Uninstalling

docs.title: Your computer
docs.text:
WhisperJAV 1.10 needs Processor x86-64 or ARM64 Linux glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, Debian 12 or newer, Fedora 36 or newer, openSUSE Leap 15.6, and distributions built on them; rolling distributions such as Arch Python 3.13 RAM 8 GB (16 GB recommended) Disk about 10 GB for the install and the models it downloads on first use NVIDIA GPU (optional) GTX 16 / RTX 20 series or newer, driver 570 or newer

Not supported (the installer says so and installs nothing): glibc older than 2.35 — Ubuntu 20.04, Debian 11, openSUSE Leap 15.5 (glibc 2.31); Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 9 (glibc 2.34). To see your glibc version: ldd --version.

AMD and Intel GPUs on Linux: in 1.10, the GGUF pipelines run on the CPU on Linux, because CrispASR publishes no Linux GPU package for AMD or Intel yet. With your own PyTorch build for your GPU (for example ROCm for an AMD GPU), the PyTorch pipelines can ask for it — see Own PyTorch.

docs.title: System packages
docs.text: Install these before the WhisperJAV installer; pip cannot install them.

docs.title: Ubuntu / Debian
docs.text:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y python3-pip python3-dev build-essential ffmpeg git
sudo apt-get install -y libsndfile1 libsndfile1-dev
# TEN VAD speech segmenter
sudo apt-get install -y libc++1 libc++abi1
# PyAudio, which auditok scene detection uses
sudo apt-get install -y portaudio19-dev
# GUI: Ubuntu 24.04+ ships WebKit 4.1, 22.04 ships 4.0; this installs whichever is there
sudo apt-get install -y libgtk-3-dev
sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev gir1.2-webkit2-4.1 \
  || sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.0-dev gir1.2-webkit2-4.0

docs.title: Fedora
docs.text:
sudo dnf install -y python3-pip python3-devel gcc gcc-c++ ffmpeg git
sudo dnf install -y libsndfile libsndfile-devel portaudio-devel
# GUI
sudo dnf install -y webkit2gtk4.1-devel gtk3-devel

On Fedora, the full ffmpeg package comes from RPM Fusion; enable RPM Fusion first if dnf does not find ffmpeg.

docs.title: Arch Linux / Manjaro
docs.text:
sudo pacman -S --noconfirm python python-pip base-devel ffmpeg git libsndfile portaudio
# GUI
sudo pacman -S --noconfirm webkit2gtk gtk3

docs.title: GUI backend (all distributions)
docs.text:
The system packages above provide WebKit, but they are not enough on their own. pywebview ships no Linux backend by default; GTK and Qt are both opt-in. And apt/dnf packages land system-wide, so a virtual environment created without --system-site-packages cannot see the gi (PyGObject) bindings.

Following the distribution instructions alone therefore still ends in ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gi' when you launch whisperjav-gui (#366). Install a backend into the virtual environment as well:

# Qt backend - simplest, needs no system GTK bindings
pip install "pywebview[qt]"

# or, to use GTK instead, expose the system bindings to the venv:
#   python3.13 -m venv --system-site-packages whisperjav-env

This step is Linux-only. Windows and macOS need nothing extra.

docs.title: Python 3.13
docs.text:
WhisperJAV 1.10 runs on Python 3.13 only. python3 --version shows your system Python; if it is not 3.13:

  • Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04: install 3.13 from the deadsnakes PPA: 
    sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y python3.13 python3.13-venv python3.13-dev
  • Fedora: sudo dnf install -y python3.13 python3.13-devel where your release offers it.
  • Any distribution: uv can download Python 3.13 for you. Install uv first (pip install --user uv, or see uv's installation page), then uv python install 3.13, then make the environment with uv venv --python 3.13 ~/.venv/whisperjav (instead of the python3.13 -m venv line below).

Then make and activate a virtual environment (Debian 12+ and Ubuntu 24.04+ do not allow installing into the system Python):

python3.13 -m venv ~/.venv/whisperjav
source ~/.venv/whisperjav/bin/activate

docs.title: NVIDIA driver
docs.text:
For the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) install you need the NVIDIA driver, 570 or newer; you do not need the CUDA Toolkit (PyTorch brings its own CUDA runtime). On Linux, 1.10 installs PyTorch for CUDA 12.8.

nvidia-smi          # shows the driver version, or fails without a driver

To install the driver:

  • Ubuntu: sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall, or sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-570, then sudo reboot.
  • Fedora: with RPM Fusion enabled, sudo dnf install -y akmod-nvidia xorg-x11-drv-nvidia-cuda, then sudo reboot.
  • Arch: sudo pacman -S nvidia nvidia-utils, then sudo reboot.
  • Data-centre GPUs (Ubuntu): sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-headless-570-server nvidia-utils-570-server, then sudo reboot.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
With the virtual environment active:

git clone --branch v1.10.2 https://github.com/meizhong986/WhisperJAV.git
cd WhisperJAV
chmod +x installer/install_linux.sh
./installer/install_linux.sh

./installer/install_linux.sh checks first that the computer is supported, then runs python3 install.py with the options you give it. python3 install.py directly does the same.

Option What it does --accelerator nvidia made for the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA 12.8 on Linux) --accelerator own-pytorch keep the PyTorch already in this environment; install everything else — experimental --accelerator cpu made for the CPU only (not accelerated) --no-speech-enhancement leave out the speech enhancement packages --minimal command line only: leaves out the GUI and, among others, the packages the WhisperSeg speech segmenter needs --dev editable install, for development --local install into .venv in the source folder even if an environment is active

(--accelerator vulkan is for Windows only: CrispASR has no Vulkan package for Linux.)

The installer installs exactly the package versions this release was tested with (uv sync from the lock file) for the accelerator of the install, and makes a GUI launcher, WhisperJAV.sh, in the source folder. Without an active environment it creates .venv in the source folder.

Users in China: the installer downloads from GitHub, PyPI, download.pytorch.org and Hugging Face. Keep your VPN on during the whole installation.

docs.title: What the install is made for
docs.text:
Without --accelerator:

  • A supported NVIDIA GPU (driver 570 or newer): made for the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA 12.8), without a question.
  • Otherwise the installer asks:
No supported NVIDIA GPU found. What should this install be made for? 1 = my own PyTorch (already installed in this Python environment, for example ROCm for an AMD GPU); 2 = CPU only (not accelerated); 3 = stop. Type 1, 2 or 3 and press Enter:

There is no time limit. With an NVIDIA GPU that 1.10 cannot use (an older card or driver), the reason is shown first. Without a console to answer (an automated run), the CPU-only install is made — or, with an NVIDIA GPU 1.10 cannot use, the installer stops.

Install made for GGUF pipelines Other pipelines NVIDIA GPU (CUDA), x86-64 NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) NVIDIA GPU (CUDA), ARM64 CPU (not accelerated) the PyTorch pipelines on the NVIDIA GPU; balanced, fast and faster on the CPU Own PyTorch CPU (not accelerated) fidelity, transformers, ChronosJAV and the speech enhancers ask for the GPU your PyTorch reports (not tested); balanced, fast and faster on the CPU unless CTranslate2, their engine, sees an NVIDIA GPU CPU only CPU (not accelerated) CPU (not accelerated), several times slower

The WhisperSeg speech segmenter runs on the CPU in every install.

docs.title: Own PyTorch
docs.text:
Install your PyTorch build into the environment first (PyTorch 2.11 is recommended; for an AMD GPU, the ROCm build from pytorch.org), then:

python3 install.py --accelerator own-pytorch

WhisperJAV installs everything except PyTorch, and never installs, replaces or removes PyTorch in this environment — not at install, upgrade or repair. Without a PyTorch in the active environment, the installer stops and installs nothing. This is experimental in 1.10.0: we could not test it; please tell us how it works: https://github.com/meizhong986/WhisperJAV/issues

The choice is recorded in whisperjav_stack.txt in the environment's folder. Running the installer again in the same environment keeps it; --accelerator chooses another.

docs.title: Check and run
docs.text:
whisperjav --check          # accelerator, where each part runs, CrispASR, models
whisperjav-gui              # or ./WhisperJAV.sh in the source folder
whisperjav video.mp4

At the start of each run, WhisperJAV says where each part runs (on an NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) install whose GPU is usable, it says nothing). --device cpu runs one job on the CPU.

On a server without a display: use the command line; the GUI packages are not needed for it.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Within 1.10, update the source code and run the installer again, with the same Python environment active as when you installed (none, if the install went into .venv); it keeps the accelerator of the environment:

git fetch --tags
git checkout v1.10.x      # the release you want
python3 install.py

A 1.9.x environment cannot be updated to 1.10: 1.10 needs Python 3.13. Make a new Python 3.13 environment and install there.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"WhisperJAV 1.10 does not support this Linux". Its glibc is older than 2.35; the message names the version. Nothing was installed. Use a newer distribution release.

The run stops: "THE NVIDIA GPU CANNOT BE USED". The install is made for the NVIDIA GPU and the GPU cannot be used now. The box names the reason (for example the driver) and the fix; --device cpu runs that one job on the CPU. nvidia-smi shows whether the driver is loaded.

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gi'. See GUI backend.

Library not found (libsndfile, portaudio, libc++). Install the system packages and run the installer again.

Git timeouts. Run the installer again; it retries with longer Git timeouts. Behind a proxy, set https_proxy before running it.

Anything else. Open an issue at GitHub Issues with the installer's output.

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
rm -rf ~/.venv/whisperjav          # the virtual environment (or the .venv in the source folder)
rm -rf ~/WhisperJAV                # the source folder, wherever you cloned it
rm -rf ~/.cache/huggingface ~/.cache/whisper   # downloaded models (optional; other programs may use them too)

Your settings are in ~/.config/WhisperJAV.

docs.title: WhisperJAV Installation Guide for Apple Silicon Macs
docs.text:
Version: 1.10.2

On an Apple silicon Mac, WhisperJAV 1.10 is installed for the Apple GPU (Metal) by itself: the GPU inside the Apple chip. Some pipelines use it, others run on the CPU (see Where each pipeline runs). There is no .exe-style installer for the Mac; you install from the source code with one script.

Nobody in the project has run WhisperJAV 1.10 on a Mac yet. The parts marked "not yet tested on a Mac" are there and should work, but we could not check them. Please tell us how it works for you: https://github.com/meizhong986/WhisperJAV/issues

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
1. Your Mac
  2. Prerequisites
  3. Installation
  4. Where each pipeline runs
  5. Running WhisperJAV
  6. Updating
  7. Troubleshooting

docs.title: 1. Your Mac
docs.text:
WhisperJAV 1.10 needs Chip Apple silicon (M1 or newer) macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer Memory 8 GB (16 GB recommended) Disk about 10 GB for the install and the models it downloads on first use Python 3.13, for Apple silicon (arm64)

Not supported (the installer says so and installs nothing): Intel Macs, because PyTorch 2.11, which WhisperJAV 1.10 needs, is not made for them; macOS 13 and older, because ONNX Runtime 1.29 needs macOS 14 or newer. A Python running under Rosetta (as an Intel program) on an Apple silicon Mac is refused too: use an arm64 Python, for example from Homebrew.

docs.title: 2. Prerequisites
docs.text:
Open Terminal and run these one by one.

  1. Xcode Command Line Tools: 
    xcode-select --install
  2. Homebrew (see brew.sh): 
    /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
  3. Python 3.13, FFmpeg, PortAudio and Git: 
    brew install python@3.13 ffmpeg portaudio git
    PortAudio is needed by PyAudio, which the auditok scene detector uses.

docs.title: 3. Installation
docs.text:
# A virtual environment with Python 3.13 (Homebrew's Python does not allow installing into it directly)
python3.13 -m venv ~/venvs/whisperjav
source ~/venvs/whisperjav/bin/activate
python3 --version          # should print Python 3.13.x

# The source code of the release
git clone --branch v1.10.2 https://github.com/meizhong986/WhisperJAV.git
cd WhisperJAV

# The installer
chmod +x installer/install_mac.sh
./installer/install_mac.sh

The script first checks that the Mac is supported (Apple silicon, macOS 14 or newer), then the Xcode tools, Homebrew, Python, FFmpeg and PortAudio, and then runs install.py. It installs exactly the package versions this release was tested with (uv sync from the lock file): PyTorch with Apple GPU support, and CrispASR's macOS build. It prints:

Apple silicon Mac: installing for the Apple GPU (Metal) — PyTorch with Apple GPU support, and CrispASR's macOS build.

At the end it creates WhisperJAV.command in the WhisperJAV folder: double-click it in Finder to start the GUI (you can drag it to the Dock).

Users in China: the installer downloads from GitHub, PyPI, download.pytorch.org and Hugging Face. Keep your VPN on during the whole installation.

Options (passed on to install.py):

Option What it does --accelerator own-pytorch keep the PyTorch already in this environment; install everything else — experimental --no-speech-enhancement leave out the speech enhancement packages --minimal command line only: leaves out the GUI and, among others, the packages the WhisperSeg speech segmenter needs --dev editable install, for development

--accelerator cpu (or the old --cpu-only) gives the same Apple GPU install: "On an Apple silicon Mac, WhisperJAV is installed for the Apple GPU (Metal), which includes the CPU. To run one job on the CPU, add --device cpu to that run."

The install's accelerator is recorded in whisperjav_stack.txt in the environment's folder.

docs.title: 4. Where each pipeline runs
docs.text:
Pipeline On an Apple silicon Mac The GGUF pipelines (parakeet, cohere, reazonspeech, kotoba, whisper-turbo, whisper-large, MOSS, haas, qwen3-asr), as Ensemble passes ask for the Apple GPU (Metal), run by CrispASR — try these first on a Mac; not yet tested on a Mac. In the GUI, choose one as pass 1 in the Ensemble Mode tab (Cohere-CrispASR is its default). They write Japanese subtitles; for English, translate them with AI translation. transformers the Apple GPU (Metal). For English subtitles, make Japanese subtitles first and translate them with AI translation: with its default model (Kotoba-Whisper bilingual), it cannot do Direct to English. fidelity asks PyTorch for the Apple GPU (Metal); its word timestamps use a fix (new in 1.10.3) that has not been tested on a Mac yet. If it fails, untick word timestamps or try a GGUF pipeline. balanced, fast, faster the CPU (not accelerated), several times slower: their engine (CTranslate2) cannot use the Apple GPU ChronosJAV (Qwen3-ASR, anime-whisper) the CPU (not accelerated) in 1.10: its ASR model does not use the Apple GPU yet WhisperSeg speech segmenter the CPU, in every install

When the Apple GPU can be used, nothing is shown at the start of a run; each pipeline says in the console where it runs as it starts (for example, balanced, fast and faster say they run on the CPU). If the Apple GPU cannot be used, a box at the start says where each part runs. The installer ends with:

On an Apple silicon Mac, try the GGUF pipelines first: choose one as pass 1 in the Ensemble Mode tab (Cohere-CrispASR is its default). CrispASR runs them on the Apple GPU (Metal). They write Japanese subtitles; for English, translate them with AI translation.

docs.title: 5. Running WhisperJAV
docs.text:
Activate the environment first (source ~/venvs/whisperjav/bin/activate), or double-click WhisperJAV.command for the GUI.

whisperjav-gui                                  # the GUI
whisperjav video.mp4 --ensemble --pass1-pipeline cohere-crispasr   # a GGUF pipeline, on the Apple GPU (try first)
whisperjav video.mp4 --mode transformers        # on the Apple GPU
whisperjav video.mp4                            # balanced, on the CPU
whisperjav --check                              # accelerator, where each part runs, CrispASR, models
whisperjav video.mp4 --device cpu               # this run on the CPU

The GUI uses macOS's own WebKit; nothing else needs installing for it.

docs.title: 6. Updating
docs.text:
Within 1.10, update the source code and run the installer again:

source ~/venvs/whisperjav/bin/activate
cd WhisperJAV
git fetch --tags
git checkout v1.10.x      # the release you want
./installer/install_mac.sh

A 1.9.x environment cannot be updated to 1.10: 1.10 needs Python 3.13. Make a new Python 3.13 environment and install there.

docs.title: 7. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"WhisperJAV 1.10 does not support Intel Macs" / "does not support macOS …". The Mac is outside the supported list; nothing was installed.

"Python 3.x is not supported". Activate the Python 3.13 environment (section 3) and run the script again.

externally-managed-environment. You ran it with Homebrew's Python directly. Make and activate a virtual environment (section 3).

PyAudio / PortAudio errors. brew install portaudio, then run the installer again.

FFmpeg not found. brew install ffmpeg, then open a new Terminal.

Slow processing. Most pipelines run on the CPU on a Mac (section 4). For the Apple GPU, use a GGUF pipeline (Ensemble Mode tab, pass 1) or the transformers pipeline.

fidelity fails on the Apple GPU. Untick word timestamps, or try a GGUF pipeline.

The GUI does not open. Check that python3 -c "import webview" works in the environment; if not, run xcode-select --install and the installer again. The command line works without the GUI.

Anything else. Open an issue at GitHub Issues with the installer's output.

Your settings are in ~/Library/Application Support/WhisperJAV.

docs.title: WhisperJAV 1.10.2 — Windows Installation from Source (Python)
docs.text: This guide installs WhisperJAV from its source code into a Python environment you manage. If you just want it to work, use the Windows Installer instead.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
1. What you need
  2. Get the source code
  3. Choose the Python environment
  4. Run the installer
  5. What the install is made for
  6. Check and run
  7. Updating
  8. Troubleshooting

docs.title: 1. What you need
docs.text:
Software Version Where to get it Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (x86-64); Windows on ARM is not supported — Python 3.13 (other versions are refused) python.org or conda/Miniconda Git any recent version git-scm.com FFmpeg 8.x, on your PATH gyan.dev, or winget install --id=Gyan.FFmpeg -e Visual C++ Redistributable 2015–2022 (x64) microsoft.com WebView2 Runtime any, for the GUI microsoft.com NVIDIA driver 580 or newer, for the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) install nvidia.com/drivers

Check them in a Command Prompt:

python --version
git --version
ffmpeg -version
nvidia-smi

nvidia-smi fails without an NVIDIA GPU; that is fine. The installer installs uv (the package installer it uses) itself if it is missing.

Users in China: the installer downloads from GitHub, PyPI, download.pytorch.org and Hugging Face. Keep your VPN on during the whole installation.

docs.title: 2. Get the source code
docs.text:
git clone --branch v1.10.2 https://github.com/meizhong986/WhisperJAV.git
cd WhisperJAV

Keep the folder path short, in plain Western letters, without spaces if you can.

docs.title: 3. Choose the Python environment
docs.text:
The installer installs into the Python environment that is active when you run it:

  • A venv: 
    python -m venv whisperjav-env
whisperjav-env\Scripts\activate
  • A conda environment: 
    conda create -n whisperjav python=3.13 -y
conda activate whisperjav
  • No active environment: the installer creates .venv inside the WhisperJAV folder and installs there. --local does the same even when an environment is active.

Never install into your system-wide Python.

docs.title: 4. Run the installer
docs.text:
From the WhisperJAV folder, with the environment active:

installer\install_windows.bat

or, the same:

python install.py
Option What it does --accelerator nvidia made for the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) --accelerator vulkan made for GPU through Vulkan (AMD, Intel or older NVIDIA card) — experimental --accelerator own-pytorch keep the PyTorch already in this environment; install everything else — experimental --accelerator cpu made for the CPU only (not accelerated) --no-speech-enhancement leave out the speech enhancement packages --minimal command line only: leaves out the GUI and, among others, the packages the WhisperSeg speech segmenter needs --dev editable install, for development --local install into .venv in the source folder even if an environment is active --log-file PATH write the log to PATH

The installer first checks that the computer is supported, then installs exactly the package versions this release was tested with (uv sync from the lock file), for the accelerator of the install. It never rewrites the lock file.

docs.title: 5. What the install is made for
docs.text:
Without --accelerator:

  • A supported NVIDIA GPU (GTX 16 / RTX 20 or newer, driver 580 or newer): made for the NVIDIA GPU (CUDA 13.0), without a question.
  • Otherwise the installer asks the same question as the Windows installer's window:
Type 1 = AMD, 2 = Intel, 3 = older NVIDIA card, 4 = my own PyTorch, 5 = CPU only, 6 = stop, then Enter:

1, 2 and 3 make the install for GPU through Vulkan; it needs the Vulkan runtime (vulkan-1.dll), which comes with your graphics driver — without it, the CPU-only install is made. With an NVIDIA GPU that 1.10 cannot use (an older card or driver), the reason is shown first. There is no time limit. 6 stops without installing anything. - No console to answer (an automated run): the CPU-only install without a supported NVIDIA GPU; a stop with an NVIDIA GPU that 1.10 cannot use.

What each accelerator gives each pipeline: Accelerated or not.

Own PyTorch. Install your PyTorch build into the environment first (PyTorch 2.11 is recommended), then run python install.py --accelerator own-pytorch. WhisperJAV installs everything except PyTorch and never installs, replaces or removes PyTorch in this environment. Without a PyTorch in the active environment, the installer stops and installs nothing.

The choice is recorded in whisperjav_stack.txt in the environment's folder. Running the installer again in the same environment keeps it; --accelerator chooses another.

docs.title: 6. Check and run
docs.text:
With the environment active:

whisperjav --check
whisperjav-gui
whisperjav video.mp4

whisperjav --check lists the accelerator of the install, where each part runs, CrispASR and the models. At the start of each run, WhisperJAV says where each part runs (on an NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) install whose GPU is usable, it says nothing). --device cpu runs one job on the CPU.

docs.title: 7. Updating
docs.text:
Within 1.10, update the source code and run the installer again, with the same Python environment active as when you installed (none, if the install went into .venv); it keeps the accelerator of the environment:

git fetch --tags
git checkout v1.10.x
python install.py

(v1.10.x stands for the release you want.) A 1.9.x environment cannot be updated to 1.10: 1.10 needs Python 3.13. Make a new Python 3.13 environment and install there.

Do not update with a plain pip install -U whisperjav…: on Windows, PyPI serves the CPU-only build of PyTorch, so it can replace your GPU build without a word.

docs.title: 8. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"WhisperJAV 1.10 does not support …". The computer is outside the supported list; the message says why. Nothing was installed.

The installer refuses your Python. WhisperJAV 1.10 needs Python 3.13. Make a 3.13 environment (section 3).

--accelerator own-pytorch stops: "none was found". Install your PyTorch and torchaudio into the active environment first, then run the installer again.

The run stops: "THE NVIDIA GPU CANNOT BE USED". The install is made for the NVIDIA GPU and the GPU cannot be used now (for example a driver change). The box names the reason and the fix; --device cpu runs that one job on the CPU.

The GGUF pipelines stop: "CrispASR could not be loaded". With the GPU-through-Vulkan or Own PyTorch install on Windows, this usually means the Vulkan runtime (vulkan-1.dll) is missing: update the graphics driver, or run python install.py --accelerator cpu.

ffmpeg not found. Put FFmpeg's bin folder on your PATH and open a new Command Prompt.

The GUI does not open. Install WebView2. To see the error, run python -m whisperjav.webview_gui.main.

Anything else. The log names the step that failed. Open an issue at GitHub Issues with it.

docs.title: WhisperJAV Windows Installer Guide
docs.text: Version: 1.10.2 Installer: WhisperJAV-1.10.2-Windows-x86_64.exe (no administrator rights needed)

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
1. Before you install
  2. Installation steps

  5. Checking your installation
  6. Coming from 1.9.x
  7. Updating within 1.10
  8. Running the installer again

  10. Troubleshooting
